intended_object: The bottom-right d × r block of a (u+d) × (l+r) matrix, i.e. its entries A(u+i, l+j) (taken from the docstring and name).
explanation: The definition is subDown (subRight A). subRight keeps the columns Fin.natAdd l j = l + j (the last r columns), and subDown keeps the rows Fin.natAdd u i = u + i (the last d rows). So entry (i, j) of the result is A (u+i) (l+j), which is exactly the bottom-right block the docstring describes. Edge cases where d or r is 0 just give an empty matrix. The entry type α is arbitrary. The Fin indexing is the point of the definition, since it splits matrices with natural-number dimensions by position. The general block notion for sum-indexed matrices is Matrix.toBlocks₂₂, but a Fin (u+d)-indexed matrix is not literally sum-indexed (it would need reindexing via finSumFinEquiv). So this is a legitimate convenience definition for a different indexing, not a narrower duplicate.
